gazetteer_names_needed.name: Camerino
gazetteer_names_needed.hint: town and Lombard/Frankish duchy and march in the Marche, about 13.07 E 43.14 N; the 883 gain is resolved meanwhile through the province of Macerata

gaps.what: The duchy continues to 1201-1226 as an imperial then papal fief (Alberic I, Boniface I, Theobald, Berengar II about 949, 967 union with Capua and Benevento, 989 Hugh of Tuscany, 1003 Tuscany, 1056 Victor II, 1155 Barbarossa, 1201 Otto IV, 1226 Berthold); Cliopatria has no shape after 898 and the dossier stops there.
Growth of the shape between 577 (15.8k km2) and 741 (22.8k km2) and the loss of its northern strip by 775 are undated; the 778-841 and 842-859 gap keyframes are borrowed shapes.

Growth 577 to 741 (Capua, Crotone, Apulia), loss of Chieti in 778, loss of Apulia in 880, and Capua entering and leaving the shape in 990/1010/1015 are undated on every page opened (events at confidence 1); Byzantine hold on Benevento 891-895 and Guy IV's rule 895 are not on any page opened.
Theme of Longobardia article (Byzantine Apulia 876-892) would not load under three titles; the Catepanate of Italy page was used instead.

1046-1055: Cliopatria's Norman Italy shape covers Benevento while the Norman page shows it surrendering at Civitate (1053) and passing under papal suzerainty; the Principality page's 1053 account is garbled.
End year 586 is Cliopatria's; the pages date the restoration of the Lombard crown to 584 (Authari) and Gummarito to 585, and give no 586 event.
No page gives an infobox area for Benevento, Spoleto or Tuscia, so the area comparison with Cliopatria was not possible.

counterparts_needing_dossiers.name: Kingdom of the Lombards (Lombard kingdom, Cliopatria Kingdom of Italy row 587-774)
Duchy of Spoleto after 898 (march and duchy under imperial then papal rule)

problems: WebFetch returns a model-written extract of each page, not raw text; phrases quoted in notes are as the extract gave them and were not checked against the raw page. Twelve distinct pages were opened; Benevento used 10 against a budget of 9 (the Spoleto article cross-read for the 759 revolt), Spoleto 6 against 5 (Principality of Benevento cross-read for 758), Tuscia 2.

Cliopatria's Spoleto 898 shape (114k km2) is Lambert's realm (the Kingdom of Italy except the Adda-Po territory), not the duchy; the Kingdom of Italy dossier should treat 891-898 as Lambert's reign and its 898 shape (51,894 km2) as Berengar's share.
Cliopatria Norman Italy 1046..1055 (24,721 km2) overlaps Benevento's land; the Norman Italy dossier (eu-13) should arbitrate.
Cliopatria 980..989 Benevento shape keeps Benevento, Capua, Spoleto and Salerno together although the Pandulf Ironhead page partitions them in March 981; a new keyframe 981..989 corrects it.

Gap keyframes (Benevento 587-740, 750-774, 1046-1055; Spoleto 571-576, 587-740, 750-774, 778-841, 842-859, 866-874, 888-895, 896-897) carry neighbouring Cliopatria shapes under the Lombard, Frankish or Norman shapes at low confidence; they are not measured boundaries and can be dropped by a reviewer without touching the ledger.

Changes of overlord are recorded as rename events here (Spoleto 776, 789, 842; Benevento 774, 1053, 1078) because vassal events belong to the overlords' dossiers (kingdom-of-the-franks, papal-states, kingdom-of-italy), which should carry Frankish suzerainty over Benevento 787-1053, papal suzerainty 1053-1081 and Spoleto's 774-776 grant to the Church.
Counterparts kingdom-of-italy in these dossiers stand for the Lombard kingdom 587-774 and may need re-pointing after the Kingdom of Italy split.

Pages disagree on several dates (division of the principality 851 vs undated; catepanate c. 965/970 vs 999; Guy II/III numbering and death year; who held Spoleto in 894-898); see the notes fields and history/polities/_notes/eu-13-a.md.
